newsitem.title: ISRAEL: French visit to PLO Jerusalem office defies Israel.
newsitem.headline: French visit to PLO Jerusalem office defies Israel.

text.p: A junior French minister on Monday visited the PLO headquarters in Jerusalem, defying an Israeli ban on foreign officials meeting Palestinian leaders at their offices in the Arab half of the city.

French President Jacques Chirac, on a Middle East tour, sent Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare Herve Gaymard to meet Palestine Liberation Organisation executive committee member Faisal al-Husseini after Israel refused to let Foreign Minister Herve de Charette make the trip.
"I came to Orient House at the request of the French president to meet Mr Faisal Husseini and the elected Palestinian officials of Jerusalem," Gaymard told reporters after the meeting.

"But the meaning of my visit here today is...to say that as long as permanent settlement of the Palestinian question has not been achieved, the status quo applies concerning the status of Jerusalem. That is the purpose of my visit here today," he said.
Israel captured Arab East Jerusalem in the 1967 Middle East war and annexed it shortly afterward in a move the international community refused to recognise.

France decided its foreign minister would boycott the Israel leg of Chirac's trip after the Israelis refused to let him visit Orient House, which the Netanyahu administration says violates Israel-PLO peace accords.

Palestinian representative to France Leila Shahid said de Charette was due to join Chirac for a historic visit to Palestinian self-rule areas on Wednesday. He would travel by land from Jordan to the West Bank.
European Union policy is that foreign ministers should visit the Orient House, headed by Husseini, on every official visit to the Jerusalem.
The PLO regards East Jerusalem as the capital of a future Palestinian state.
Israel and the PLO have agreed in self-rule deals signed since 1993 to discuss the fate of the disputed city in talks on the final status of the areas.
Husseini said Gaymard's visit reflected France's long- standing support of the Palestinians.

"It was an important visit. The minister was an emissary of the French President Mr Jacques Chirac. He told us that France was holding to its position and that it did not change its stand towards Jerusalem," Husseini said.
